sources.title: B. H. Bowditch, Notes on locally CAT(1) spaces (Aberdeen preprint, 27 scanned sheets, two printed pages per sheet)
sources.locator: §§2–3.4, printed pp. 13–32 of the scanned preprint: local geodesics and injectivity radius (2.16); loop classes, closed local geodesics and short-loop homotopy (3.1.4–3.1.7); the product model and its curvature (3.2.1); midpoint polygons, mesh/length/energy and the equality case (3.3.1–3.3.6); the quantitative decrement, comparison disk, radius and quadrilateral estimates (3.3.8–3.3.15); the shrinkable-loop conclusions (3.4). §§3.5–3.7 and the remaining printed pages were not read.

contents.name: 2.16: local geodesics of length at most the injectivity radius are global; two local geodesics with common endpoints give a minimum embedded circle
3.1.4–3.1.5: a closed local geodesic is not homotopic to a constant through loops of length < 2π; every short loop in the constant-loop component contracts with nonincreasing length
3.1.6–3.1.7: midpoint-iteration limit classes; every loop shorter than the minimal embedded-circle length is shrinkable and the minimal embedded circle is the shortest nonshrinkable loop
3.2.1: the product model S²×S² and its curvature bound (the printed 'curvature ≤ −1' is a typo for ≤ 1)
3.3.1–3.3.4: midpoint operation; mesh, length and energy do not increase; equality exactly for constant polygons and for equally spaced vertices of a closed local geodesic
3.3.5–3.3.6: polygons with zero length limit are exactly those eventually shortened below l/2; the set is open and its iterates converge to a constant
3.3.8–3.3.9: quantitative energy decrement E(fx) ≤ E(x) − λ(L(x)) with λ positive and continuous on (0,2π) and independent of the mesh bound h
3.3.10: spherical radius estimate for loops of length 2r < 2π (radius r/2, η = (π−r)/2)
3.3.11: quadrilateral separation δ(η,μ) > 0 with the intrinsic developed-quadrilateral bound and the condition μ < 2η
3.3.12–3.3.14: the finite midpoint-operation comparison disk, its interior/boundary angle conditions and the row induction excluding simple closed local geodesics
3.3.15: closedness of the zero-limit class in the short-polygon space via the uniform iteration bound
degenerate comparison triangles: product with a small Euclidean regular polygon and passage of the decrement to the limit
3.4: passage between rectifiable loops and polygons by chord subdivision and local interpolation, with nonincreasing length
§§3.5–3.7 and the remaining printed pages: applications to particular complexes, curve-shortening flows and higher-dimensional statements
contents.reason: The later sections concern applications to particular complexes and flows; this pair needs only the general short-loop class and quantitative energy theory of §§2–3.4 and no result of §§3.5–3.7 is stated or used by any item.

contents.name: §§1 and 2 (beyond local geodesics and injectivity radius): contractibility, fixed-point and geometric-group preliminaries
contents.reason: Contractibility and fixed-point theory of locally CAT(1) spaces belong to the Davis CAT(0) geometry pair and the metric-flag pair, which consume this page's short-loop theory rather than being used by it.

sources.title: Martin R. Bridson and André Haefliger, Metric Spaces of Non-Positive Curvature (Springer Grundlehren 319, 1999; author-hosted PDF)
sources.locator: II.1.4 (unique geodesics for distances < D_κ, local geodesics of length ≤ D_κ are geodesics, convex balls of radius < D_κ/2); I.2.1–I.2.16 (the round sphere, model spaces M²_κ, laws of cosines and Alexandrov's Lemma); II.4.12–II.4.17 (compact balls, injectivity radius, systole and the minimum embedded circle); read in the extracted full text.

contents.name: I.1.1–I.1.5: local geodesics, geodesics and length in metric spaces
I.2.1–I.2.3: the round sphere Sⁿ, its metric d(A,B)=arccos(A·B), geodesics and convex balls
I.2.13–I.2.16: law of cosines in M²_κ, existence of comparison triangles, κ-comparison angles and Alexandrov's Lemma
II.1.4(1): uniqueness of geodesic segments for distances < D_κ and continuous dependence on endpoints
II.1.4(2): every local geodesic of length at most D_κ is a geodesic
II.1.4(3): balls of radius < D_κ/2 are convex with unique geodesics
II.4.12–II.4.16: compact balls, injectivity radius, systole, the minimum embedded circle and the compact short-circle criterion
I.7.39 and I.7.55–I.7.59: cone neighbourhoods, injectivity radius and systole of polyhedral complexes
II.5.15–II.5.21: flag and metric-flag complexes and Moussong's Lemma
contents.reason: The metric-flag criterion and Moussong's Lemma are the subject of the later large-spherical-metric-flags pair, which consumes this page's short-loop control; no item here states them.

sources.title: Michael W. Davis, The Geometry and Topology of Coxeter Groups (first-edition author manuscript, 2007-2008)
sources.locator: Appendix I.2.6–I.2.19, printed pp. 502–507 (contractibility, the CAT(0)-inequality I.2.15, local geodesics I.2.16, the cone on a CAT(1)-space I.2.17–I.2.18 and the κ>0 criterion I.2.8); §I.7.1 (M_κ-polyhedral vocabulary) and §7.3 (Coxeter cells) read for the metric-flag application this page feeds.

contents.name: Appendix I.2.6–I.2.8: contractibility of complete CAT(0)-spaces, Gromov's Cartan–Hadamard theorem and the curvature ≤ κ>0 criterion
Appendix I.2.15: the CAT(0)-inequality is equivalent to the hinged quadratic inequality
Appendix I.2.16: a path of length ≤ π/√κ in a CAT(κ)-space is a geodesic if and only if it is a local geodesic
Appendix I.2.10–I.2.14: centers of bounded sets, the Bruhat–Tits fixed point theorem and convex fixed-point sets
contents.reason: The fixed-point theory needs an isometric group action on a complete CAT(0) space, which is the subject of the Davis CAT(0) pair; this page has no group action and states none of it.

contents.name: Appendix I.2.17–I.2.19: the cone on a CAT(1)-space, the spherical join and joins of CAT(1)-spaces
contents.reason: Cone and join constructions are supplied by the spherical-simplex/cones pair and consumed by the CAT comparison pair; this page uses only the CAT(1) comparison inequalities of its declared prerequisite.

contents.name: §7.3 and §I.7.1: Coxeter cells, their link structure and the M_κ-polyhedral vocabulary
contents.reason: The Coxeter cell complex itself is built on coxeter-polyhedral-gluings-and-intrinsic-metrics and its metric-flag links on the large-spherical-metric-flags pair; this page supplies only the short-loop/energy control they will consume.
